content: Respiratory distress syndrome (RDS) occurs due to a deficiency or dysfunction of pulmonary surfactant, a substance critical for maintaining lung function. Various surfactant products have been developed and tested in clinical trials, including synthetic surfactants and those derived from animal sources. Surfactant replacement therapy has been used either to prevent the onset of RDS in high-risk premature infants or to treat established RDS in preterm infants. The objective of this study was to evaluate the effects of administering animal-derived surfactant extracts on mortality, chronic lung disease, and other complications associated with prematurity in preterm infants diagnosed with RDS. Subgroup analyses were planned based on the specific surfactant product used, the degree of prematurity, and the severity of the disease. The researchers conducted a comprehensive search of multiple databases, including the Oxford Database of Perinatal Trials, MEDLINE, EMBASE, and CINAHL, covering studies from 1975 to December 2008. Additional sources such as previous reviews, cross-references, conference proceedings, and expert consultations were also examined. Only randomized or quasi-randomized controlled trials comparing the effects of animal-derived surfactant extracts in infants with established RDS were included. Data on clinical outcomes were extracted from the trial reports by the review authors, and the analysis was performed according to the standards of the Cochrane Neonatal Review Group. Thirteen randomized controlled trials were included in the final analysis. The studies showed that treatment with animal-derived surfactant extracts led to an initial improvement in respiratory status, including better oxygenation and reduced need for ventilator support. The meta-analysis revealed a significant reduction in the risk of air leaks (relative risk 0.47, 95% CI 0.39–0.58), pneumothorax (relative risk 0.42, 95% CI 0.34–0.52), and pulmonary interstitial emphysema (relative risk 0.45, 95% CI 0.37–0.55). There was also a significant decrease in neonatal mortality (relative risk 0.68, 95% CI 0.57–0.82) and mortality prior to hospital discharge (relative risk 0.63, 95% CI 0.44–0.90). Additionally, the risk of bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) or death at 28 days of age was significantly reduced (relative risk 0.83, 95% CI 0.77–0.90). However, no significant differences were observed in the risks of patent ductus arteriosus, necrotizing enterocolitis, intraventricular hemorrhage, BPD, or retinopathy of prematurity. In conclusion, preterm infants with established RDS who receive treatment with animal-derived surfactant extracts experience a reduced risk of pneumothorax, pulmonary interstitial emphysema, mortality, and bronchopulmonary dysplasia or death.
